slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
Welcome to the Sommelier's Notebook! In this introductory lesson, we begin with the most fundamental question: where is Bordeaux? This seemingly simple question is the first key to understanding what makes Bordeaux wine truly great.

Geography determines everything. Bordeaux is located in southwestern France, between 44°–45° N latitude, just 60 km from the Atlantic Ocean. This unique position gives Bordeaux its mild oceanic climate, diverse soil types, and nourishment from three major rivers — the perfect combination of geographical factors that has made Bordeaux one of the world's greatest wine regions.

Learning Objectives

📍 Master Bordeaux's Geographic Location

Understand Bordeaux's exact position in France — its latitude, area, and surrounding geography

🌊 Understand How Geography Shapes Terroir

Learn how the Atlantic Ocean, the Gironde, the Garonne, and the Dordogne shape Bordeaux's climate and soils

🗺️ Identify the Major Appellations

Get an initial overview of the geographic locations of the Left Bank, Right Bank, and Entre-Deux-Mers

🏛️ Explore Bordeaux's Historic Standing

Understand Bordeaux's historical roots and strategic advantages as the wine capital of the world

After completing this lesson, you will be able to clearly describe Bordeaux's geographic location and understand how geographical factors laid the foundation for this great wine region. Let's begin this exciting journey through Bordeaux!
slides.4.title: Lesson Complete
slides.4.description: Congratulations on completing the foundational study of Bordeaux's Left Bank and Right Bank! You have now mastered the core geographic division of Bordeaux and understand how the Garonne and Dordogne rivers shape the terroir differences between the two banks. The Left Bank's gravel soils and Cabernet Sauvignon, the Right Bank's clay and Merlot — this foundational knowledge is the first key to understanding Bordeaux wine.
